tasks.short: Examine print orders and determine job requirements

steps.what: Retrieve the current job order, approved artwork reference and special printing instructions
Examine quantities, stock specifications, colors and special instructions and resolve ambiguities

tasks.design: Configure a single current job-order view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, linking artwork and instructions from {DOCS}. The operator still reads requirements and resolves ambiguity rather than treating populated fields as proof of understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current orders and amendments can be spread across paper bags and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: A native order view can reduce retrieval and version hunting.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting unusual instructions and detecting contradictory requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising implications for the actual press and materials.
tasks.altitude: Less order retrieval; interpretation and operating authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify artwork and special production requirements
reach.learn: Job-ticket version control and specification completeness

evidence.claim: MultiPress includes order forms and stock functions, supporting central job information without proving interpretation savings.
The retrieval saving is an E1 task scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is retrieval and understanding of an issued order, excluding original order capture, physical material inspection and terminal settings entry.

Existing order coordinator produces job identifier, revision, quantity, stock, colors, special instructions and approved-artwork reference in the unchanged order-release process. Operator checks missing versions or fields manually within s1's ten retained hours.

Test native order views first; no new upstream structured capture is required for the central scenario. If orders remain unstructured, read them manually rather than presume an extracted specification.
Two incremental operator hours per 100 baseline hours cover broken references and view checks.
unknowns: Current ticket completeness and time spent retrieving revisions
research_questions: Does one current-order view reduce retrieval after missing-field checks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90; gross10 less2 upkeep gives8 net. Existing well-organised job packs may save only2 retrieval hours and net zero; requirement examination retains80.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify paper and ink meet print-job specifications

steps.what: Verify physical paper and ink identity, condition and suitability against job specifications

tasks.design: Keep physical paper and ink verification with the operator using the current specification in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Artwork comparison tools do not establish that actual stock or ink is suitable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material labels and system records do not guarantee physical condition or suitability.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible specifications support checking without replacing the physical inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting wrong stock, contamination or unsuitable ink condition.
tasks.human_edge: Comparing physical materials with the job and recognising exceptions.
tasks.altitude: Material verification time and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess a disputed paper or ink exception

evidence.claim: Retaining physical paper and ink verification is an E1 judgement; file proofing does not establish this capability.

assumptions: Boundary is physical material verification, excluding order interpretation and separate inventory posting.
Operator observes identity and condition directly in retained s1; no free structured suitability flag or assumed sensor verdict exists.
No new system is introduced and incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Material acceptance requirements and available test equipment
research_questions: Which material exceptions need quality-technician assessment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross0 and net0. Physical verification is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor automated press operation and respond to alerts

steps.what: Monitor automated press operation and interpret fault, error and alert messages
Respond to press faults and alerts using approved procedures and verify safe recovery

tasks.design: Retain monitoring and recovery decisions at the {OTHER} press control system. Existing alarm handling and safety interlocks remain part of the current machine, without being credited as newly saved operator labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: An alert requires interpretation alongside actual machine behaviour.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controls identify faults but do not establish unattended recovery.
tasks.still_hard: Determining the cause and whether intervention or escalation is safe.
tasks.human_edge: Situational awareness and responsible fault response.
tasks.altitude: No change to monitoring coverage or recovery authority.

reach.learn: Safe isolation and useful fault descriptions

evidence.claim: Retaining press monitoring and safe fault response is an E1 judgement; the digest concerns job flow and file checking.

assumptions: Boundary is operator monitoring and response, excluding machine controller runtime and specialist repair.

Existing press controller produces alerts during unchanged operation; operator validates their meaning against the machine in fully retained s1. No new error code or fault classification must be captured for automation.
No control retrofit or additional workflow is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Press control features, response procedures and maintenance boundaries
research_questions: Which alerts require stopping and escalating rather than operator recovery?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross0 and net0. Existing automatic control runtime is excluded from savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Input production settings into printing-system terminals

steps.what: Check job settings against the approved ticket and approve the exact terminal payload
Input the approved production job settings into the press workstation terminal
Read back terminal settings and resolve any difference before allowing separate press startup

tasks.design: Test a native ticket-import connection from {OPS_SYSTEM} to the {OTHER} press workstation before custom integration. Import only the approved settings payload, retain read-back checks, and keep physical startup outside this transfer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operators retype structured job settings already available in released tickets.
tasks.enabler_now: Compatible press interfaces can import mapped settings deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Machine-specific units, presets and changes between ticket revisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising settings that are unsuitable for the actual press or materials.
tasks.altitude: Less settings re-entry; approval, read-back and startup authority stay with the operator.

reach.learn: Unit conversion, preset versions and import validation

evidence.claim: Compatible structured print-ticket import is an E1 design assumption from model knowledge; the digest's print MIS case does not verify this press interface or saving.

assumptions: Boundary is checking, entering and verifying job settings, excluding upstream ticket creation, physical setup and press startup.

Existing prepress technician produces released job identifier, revision, quantity, stock identifier, color profile, imposition reference and press preset in unchanged ticket preparation. No new upstream fields are assumed; unsupported or unstructured tickets stay manual with no central saving.

Operator verifies target press, units, mapped fields and preset revision in fully retained s1, producing the exact approved payload consumed by s2. S3 retains full read-back and manual correction; import cannot start the press.

Test native import first. Four incremental operator hours per 100 baseline hours cover mapping checks and transfer failures; any new prepress mapping upkeep is counted separately as two other-role hours.
unknowns: Press import support, ticket structure and existing re-entry time
research_questions: Can the press import exactly approved settings without startup and with reliable read-back?

approvals.approved_version: Exact job revision, target terminal, field values, units and preset version approved in s1; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R50; gross50 less4 focal upkeep gives46 net when native import fits. Unsupported tickets retain all entry and may lose4 to upkeep; two other-role upkeep hours are excluded from focal saving but must remain in team costs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated ticket retrieval and supported terminal entry while preserving inspection and fault response.
role.ambitious_version: Load verified settings once on compatible presses and retain direct control over production safety and quality.
